relations.subject: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé
relations.evidence: Duyvendak's Chinese assistant Chang T'ien-tse, a native of Fujian Province, provided them with instruction in modern Mandarin Chinese as well as some basic training in Hokkien Chinese

relations.subject: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé
relations.evidence: While in Beijing, Hulsewé's instructor in Classical Chinese was Liang Qixiong (梁啟雄; 1900–1965), a scholar and the younger brother of famed Chinese writer Liang Qichao.

relations.subject: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé
relations.evidence: In 1946, after the end of the war, Hulsewé returned to the Netherlands, where Duyvendak offered him a position as a lecturer in Chinese at Leiden, which he accepted.

relations.subject: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé
relations.evidence: Following Duyvendak's death in 1954, Hulsewé was chosen in 1956 to succeed him as Professor of Chinese at Leiden, a position he held until his retirement in 1975.

relations.subject: Marius van der Valk
relations.evidence: His only classmate during his first year was Marius van der Valk (1908–1978), who studied Chinese and law, and later became a professor of modern Chinese law at Leiden.
